'''Walter Taylor''' ({{c.|1700}} – 23 February 1743/44) was a [[Trinity College, Cambridge]] mathematics tutor who coached 83 students in the 1724&ndash;1743 period. He later was appointed as the [[Regius Professor of Greek (Cambridge)|Regius Professor of Greek]].

He was the son of John Taylor, Vicar of [[Tuxford]], [[Nottinghamshire]]. He matriculated in 1716 from [[Queen Elizabeth Grammar School, Wakefield|Wakefield School]], [[Yorkshire]]. Taylor was admitted as a [[pensioner]] at Trinity on 7 April 1716.<ref name=Venn>{{acad|id=TLR716W|name=Taylor, Walter}}</ref>

[[Robert Smith (mathematician)|Robert Smith]] was Taylor's Cambridge tutor.

==Timeline==
* 1717 Scholar
* 1719/20 BA
* 1723 MA
* 1736 BD
* 1722 Fellow of Trinity
* 1726–44 Regius Professor of Greek
* 1725 Ordained deacon
* 1726/7 Ordained priest
* 1743/4 buried at [[Tuxford]]
